<system-reminder>
## Swarm Mode

You are now in "agent swarm" mode. The user may send tasks that require a large number of parallel subagents.

## Workflow

You do not need to use TodoList to record this workflow.

1. First, you may need to do a small amount of exploratory work before deciding how to divide the task across subagents. You may not need subagents during this exploratory phase.

2. After exploring, if you are convinced no subagent is needed to complete the task, tell the user why and wait for further instructions; otherwise, continue with the appropriate delegation.

3. Once you have enough context, do not handle the main work yourself. Use AgentSwarm with a `prompt_template` containing the `{{item}}` placeholder and an `items` array for the requested or appropriate number of subagents, partitioning the problem so each item gives one subagent a distinct part of the work. Pass `subagent_type` when the whole swarm should use a non-default subagent profile.

## Coordination

- Give each subagent a distinct scope of work.
- Avoid duplicating work across subagents.
- Avoid assigning conflicting changes or responsibilities to different subagents.
- Remember that subagents have your full capabilities. Do not overload their prompts with excessive detail; only describe the necessary background and each subagent's specific task.
- Unless the user explicitly specifies a lower limit, do not try to conserve the number of agents. AgentSwarm supports up to 128 subagents and queues launches automatically, so decompose work as finely as possible while keeping subagent responsibilities non-conflicting; combine tasks only when they are genuinely inseparable. If the subagents only need to read, inspect, or report back without making changes, their scopes may overlap slightly.
</system-reminder>

This is an operating-systems course lab (Projects 1–6) that implements a RISC-V bare-metal operating system. The repo spans six incremental projects: a bootloader, a simple cooperative kernel, a preemptive kernel with SMP, an interactive OS with process management and IPC, a virtual-memory-enabled kernel with demand paging, a device-driver layer with network support, and a file system. Entire subsystems have been removed and must be re-implemented.

Your working directory is `/workspace`. The project code is already present in seven subdirectories: `Project1-Bootloader`, `Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part1`, `Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part2`, `Project3-Interactive_OS_and_Process_Management`, `Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management`, `Project5-Device_Driver`, and `Project6-File_System`.

Implement the following modules:

The following modules need to be implemented or substantially built out. All stubbed function bodies contain `/* TODO: implement */`.

Bootloader Image Builder (`Project1-Bootloader/createimage.c`): The host-side tool that reads ELF binaries and writes a bootable disk image. Two functions handle segment writing and OS size recording. (~1 file, 2 functions to implement)

Part 1 Scheduler & Locking (`Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part1/kernel/sched/sched.c`, `kernel/locking/lock.c`): The cooperative round-robin scheduler, task blocking/unblocking primitives, and mutex lock acquire/release. (~2 files, 5 functions to implement)

Part 2 Scheduler & Synchronisation (`Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part2/kernel/`): The preemptive priority-based scheduler with ready-queue management, priority-based task selection, timer expiration checking, mutex locking, binary semaphore operations, and futex wait/wakeup with hash-based node management. (~5 files, 9 functions to implement)

Process Management & IPC (`Project3-Interactive_OS_and_Process_Management/kernel/`): Multi-core scheduler with process lifecycle management (spawn, exit, kill, waitpid), priority-based scheduling with CPU affinity masks, binary semaphore tracking, and a mailbox-based inter-process communication system for sending and receiving messages with blocking semantics. (~4 files, 12 functions to implement)

Virtual Memory Management (`Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/kernel/mm/mm.c`, `kernel/sched/sched.c`): SV39 three-level page table initialisation and teardown, user page allocation with NRU page replacement, swap-to-disk eviction, demand-paging page fault handling, shared memory mapping/unmapping, process creation/execution with ELF loading, and process termination with resource cleanup. (~2 files, 13 functions to implement)

Device Driver Layer (`Project5-Device_Driver/drivers/net.c`, `kernel/mm/mm.c`, `kernel/sched/sched.c`): Network packet send/receive with poll and interrupt modes, IRQ mode switching, plus the full virtual memory and scheduler subsystems carried forward from Project 4 with additional page-helper functionality. (~3 files, 18 functions to implement)

File System (`Project6-File_System/kernel/fs/`): A complete on-disk file system with superblock/bitmap-based allocation, inode and block management (alloc, free), directory operations (mkdir, rmdir, ls, cd), hard/soft linking, file operations (touch, cat, fopen, fread, fwrite), plus the full scheduler and virtual memory subsystems from Project 5. `void do_scheduler(void)` (P2A) — cooperative round-robin scheduler
`void do_block(list_node_t *pcb_node, list_head *queue)` (P2A) — moves a PCB to a block queue
`void do_unblock(list_node_t *pcb_node)` (P2A) — moves a PCB back to the ready queue
`void do_mutex_lock_acquire(mutex_lock_t *lock)` (P2A, P2B) — acquires a mutex with blocking
`void do_mutex_lock_release(mutex_lock_t *lock)` (P2A, P2B) — releases a mutex and wakes waiters
`void scheduler(void)` (P2B, P3, P4, P5, P6) — preemptive priority-based scheduler
`list_node_t* max_priority_node(void)` (P2B, P3, P4, P5, P6) — selects the highest-priority ready task
`pid_t do_spawn(task_info_t *task, void *arg, spawn_mode_t mode)` (P3) — creates a new process
`void do_exit()` (P3, P4, P5, P6) — handles process exit and resource cleanup
`int do_kill(pid_t pid)` (P3, P4, P5, P6) — terminates a process by PID
`int do_waitpid(pid_t pid, ...)` (P3, P4, P5, P6) — waits for a child process to exit

`ptr_t selete_page(void)` (P4, P5, P6) — NRU page replacement to select a victim page
`void write_to_sd(ptr_t pa)` (P4, P5, P6) — evicts a page to disk swap space

`uintptr_t shm_page_get(int key)` (P4, P5, P6) — maps a shared memory page into the current process
`void shm_page_dt(uintptr_t addr)` (P4, P5, P6) — unmaps a shared memory page
`void handle_page_fault(regs_context_t *regs, uint64_t stval, uint64_t cause)` (P4, P5, P6) — demand-paging page fault handler
`long do_net_recv(uintptr_t addr, size_t length, int num_packet, size_t *frLength)` (P5) — receives network packets
`void do_net_send(uintptr_t addr, size_t length)` (P5) — sends a network packet
`void do_net_irq_mode(int mode)` (P5) — switches between poll and interrupt modes
`uint16_t alloc_inode()` (P6) — allocates a free inode from the bitmap
`uint32_t alloc_block()` (P6) — allocates a free block from the bitmap
`void free_inode(uint16_t inode_id)` (P6) — frees an inode in the bitmap
`void free_block(uint32_t block_id)` (P6) — frees a block in the bitmap
`int mkfs(int print)` (P6) — initialises the file system superblock and root directory
`int do_mkdir(char *dirname)` (P6) — creates a new directory
`int do_rmdir(char *dirname)` (P6) — removes a directory
`int do_ls(char *dirname, int mode, int *print_location_y)` (P6) — lists directory contents
`int do_cd(char *dirname)` (P6) — changes the current working directory
`int do_link(char *filename, char *newfile, int mode)` (P6) — creates hard or soft links
`int do_touch(char *filename)` (P6) — creates a new empty file
`int do_cat(char *filename, char *buffer)` (P6) — reads file contents into a buffer
`int do_fopen(char *filename, int access)` (P6) — opens a file and returns a file descriptor
`int do_fread(int fd, char *buffer, int size)` (P6) — reads data from an open file
`int do_fwrite(int fd, char *buffer, int size)` (P6) — writes data to an open file
`int do_mbox_open(char *name)` (P3) — opens or creates a named mailbox
`int do_mbox_send(int mailbox_id, void *msg, int msg_length)` (P3) — sends a message to a mailbox
`int do_mbox_recv(int mailbox_id, void *msg, int msg_length)` (P3) — receives a message from a mailbox
`void binsem_op(int binsem_id, int op)` (P2B, P3) — performs lock/unlock on a binary semaphore
`futex_node_t* get_node(volatile uint64_t *val_addr, int create)` (P2B) — looks up or creates a futex node
`void futex_wait(volatile uint64_t *val_addr, uint64_t val)` (P2B) — blocks on a futex if value matches
`void futex_wakeup(volatile uint64_t *val_addr, int num_wakeup)` (P2B) — wakes tasks blocked on a futex
`void timer_check(void)` (P2B) — checks expired timers and invokes callbacks
`pid_t do_exec(const char *file_name, int argc, char *argv[], spawn_mode_t mode)` (P4, P5, P6) — loads and executes an ELF binary as a new process
`uintptr_t alloc_page_helper(uintptr_t va, uintptr_t pgdir)` (P5, P6) — allocates a page and maps it at a virtual address

# UCAS OS
本仓库是中国科学院大学操作系统研讨课的实验内容。本研讨课的实验基于RISC-V指令集，逐步实现了操作系统启动、进程调度和管理、虚拟内存、网卡驱动、文件系统等内容。


## 目录结构
将六个实验项目组织为了七个文件夹，其中第二个实验项目比较困难因此分为了两部分。后面的实验项目的完成过程中只对前面的实验项目的代码做了少量修改，基本没有删减功能。（例如Project3-6仍基于双核完成）。
1. Project1-Bootloader
2. Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part1
3. Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part2
4. Project3-Interactive_OS_and_Process_Management
5. Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management
6. Project5-Device_Driver
7. Project6-File_System


## 开发环境
本实验用到的RISC-V开发板是XILINX PYNQ Z2开发板，开发板上有ARM核和FPGA，RISC-V核烧写到FPGA中。在开发板上电时由ARM核启动相关程序(BOOT.bin)，将RISC-V核烧入FPGA。之后，RISC-V核自动加载相关程序。RISC-V核为采用SiFive开源的Rocket核心。其基本信息为：
1. RV64IMAFDC(GC)指令集
2. 双核五级流水处理器
3. 数据/指令缓存大小各为16KB，4路组相联
4. 时钟频率为100MHz

另外我们需要一张SD卡。将SD卡格式化为两个分区：第一个分区34MB，采用fat32文件系统；剩余空间全部划入第二个分区，保持第二个分区为空分区。制作完以后，将预先提供的BOOT.bin和RV_BOOT.bin拷入到第一个分区。

## 运行方法
拿到裸开发板以后，需要将开发板按如下方式配置：
1. 将开发板设置为SD卡启动。PYNQ Z2支持从SD、QSPI和JTAG启动。我们将跳线插到最左侧，选择用SD卡启动。
2. 设置电源选项。PYNQ Z2支持电源供电和Micro-USB供电。我们把跳线插到USB这个选项上，用Micro-USB直接供电。

配置完开发板后，可以按照各实验项目中的README进行操作。


## 实验总结
虽然完成了Project1-5的C-Core和Project6的A-Core，但还是有一些地方因为时间关系没来得及完成，算是留下了一些遗憾。
1. Project6的代码应该可以运行C-Core的测试程序，但因为需要修改发包程序等而没有进行测试。
2. Project6中关于文件系统的系统调用中的路径查找操作可以提取出来，形成一个单独的函数。
3. Project6中软链接的实现共用了文件的数据块，不符合设计要求。
4. Project5中网卡驱动的代码有很多冗余，可以删除部分无用代码让这一部分变得更优美。
5. 部分需要在Shell中输出的系统调用的实现方式为用户态传入buffer的地址，内核将打印的内容填入buffer中让用户打印。但这种实现方式非常不优美，可以用prints完成一样的功能。
6. 使用prints在Shell中输出的系统调用可能会打印超出屏幕边界。
7. 进程只能阻塞在用户态：进程被解除阻塞后只能从用户态的代码开始执行。这一feature造成waitpid系统调用实现困难，因为父进程在子进程结束时被解除阻塞，此时父进程还要回收子进程的内核栈和PCB，但父进程被解除阻塞后只能从用户态的代码开始执行，没有机会进行回收操作。本人的waitpid系统调用实现非常tricky。
8. 大部分系统调用没有进行参数检查。
9. 双核运行的情况下进程两次获取当前的tick数可能获取到不同核的数据，造成时间测量精度差。
10. 与体系结构相关的代码，特别是虚存管理部分的代码，没有写在arch/riscv目录下。
11. 不能从SD卡的文件中加载可执行程序，可执行程序只能随内核一起编译并附带在内核中。
12. 很多文件include了一些不必要的头文件，头文件的引用也有不规范的地方。

You are implementing part of a RISC-V bare-metal OS course repo (UCAS OS) at /workspace. The repo contains 7 self-contained project directories (Project1-Bootloader, Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part1, Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part2, Project3-Interactive_OS_and_Process_Management, Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management, Project5-Device_Driver, Project6-File_System), each a snapshot of an evolving dual-core Rocket-chip OS. This is a well-known course codebase; implement the standard, correct version of each function, not placeholders.

Global rules:
- Modify ONLY the files assigned to you. Other subagents are concurrently implementing other files and other project directories — do not touch their files, and do not copy from another project directory that may itself still be stubbed (treat other directories as reference for design intent only, never as a dependency).
- NEVER run any git command (no add/commit/checkout/diff/stash). The parent agent handles all git operations.
- Keep every existing function signature exactly as-is. Do not rename, remove, or change visibility of any existing function or global.
- Read first: the stub file itself, its headers (include/, arch/riscv/include/), the syscall dispatch table, and callers, before writing code.
- Toolchain: the installed cross compiler is riscv64-linux-gnu-* but Makefiles default to a prefix that is not installed. Build with an override such as `make CROSS_PREFIX=riscv64-linux-gnu-` (check the Makefile for the actual variable name first). Known pre-existing issue: in P2-P6 the pre-filled createimage tool may segfault at the final `./createimage` image-creation step with this toolchain — that is unrelated to your work; in that case verify with the kernel-binary target instead (e.g. `make CROSS_PREFIX=riscv64-linux-gnu- main`), and do NOT "fix" pre-filled files unless they are assigned to you.
- Success criteria: (1) every `/* TODO: implement */` stub in your assigned files is fully implemented with correct logic; (2) the project still compiles with your changes (warnings OK, errors not). Re-run the build after your edits and iterate until it compiles.
- If the project's build system generates artifacts (image, main, *.o), leave them; do not clean them away at the end.
- When finished, report concisely: files changed, functions implemented (one line each on what the logic does), the build command used and its result, and any assumptions or concerns.

YOUR ASSIGNMENT:

ASSIGNED FILES: /workspace/Project1-Bootloader/createimage.c (the ONLY file you may modify).
Task: Bootloader image builder (host-side tool, compiled with host gcc, run as `./createimage --extended bootblock kernel`). Implement the two stubs: `static void write_segment(Elf64_Phdr phdr, FILE *fp, FILE *img, int *nbytes)` and `static void write_os_size(int nbytes, FILE *img)`.
Semantics: write_segment copies one loadable ELF segment from fp into img at the current image offset, padding up to a 512-byte boundary (sectors), and advances *nbytes by the padded byte count. write_os_size records the OS size in sectors at byte offset 508 of the image (the bootblock reads the sector count there) — see the reference implementation in /workspace/Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part1/tools/createimage.c (read-only reference, do NOT modify it): it rounds memsz up to 512, writes the segment bytes, and writes `nbytes/512 - 1` as a 2-byte value at offset 508.
Robustness requirement: the installed riscv64-linux-gnu-gcc emits extra non-PT_LOAD program headers (PHDR, INTERP, DYNAMIC, GNU_STACK, and zero-memsz ones) that make the naive reference implementation crash. Your implementation MUST: only write segments with p_type == PT_LOAD and p_memsz > 0, and copy via a fixed-size buffer loop (e.g. 512-byte chunks, zero-padding the final partial sector) rather than a variable-length array. Keep the printed output format consistent with the surrounding code.
Verify: cd /workspace/Project1-Bootloader && make CC=riscv64-linux-gnu-gcc must complete and produce ./image without crashing; then confirm with `xxd -s 508 -l 4 image` that a plausible non-zero sector count was written at offset 508, and that the image size is a multiple of 512.

- lock.c: `void do_mutex_lock_acquire(mutex_lock_t *lock)` — if the lock is held, block the current task on the lock's block queue and re-check after being woken (loop until acquired); set lock owner/status per the struct definition; `void do_mutex_lock_release(mutex_lock_t *lock)` — release the lock and wake waiter(s) per the existing design (check how many the tests/headers expect — look at the block queue handling).

- binsem.c: `void binsem_op(int binsem_id, int op)` — BINSEM_OP_LOCK: block current task if the semaphore is taken; BINSEM_OP_UNLOCK: release and wake a waiter (constants in headers).

YOUR ASSIGNMENT:
ASSIGNED FILES: /workspace/Project1-Bootloader/createimage.c (the ONLY file you may modify).
Task: Bootloader image builder (host-side tool, compiled with host gcc, run as `./createimage --extended bootblock kernel`). Implement the two stubs: `static void write_segment(Elf64_Phdr phdr, FILE *fp, FILE *img, int *nbytes)` and `static void write_os_size(int nbytes, FILE *img)`.
Semantics: write_segment copies one loadable ELF segment from fp into img at the current image offset, padding up to a 512-byte boundary (sectors), and advances *nbytes by the padded byte count. write_os_size records the OS size in sectors at byte offset 508 of the image (the bootblock reads the sector count there) — see the reference implementation in /workspace/Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part1/tools/createimage.c (read-only reference, do NOT modify it): it rounds memsz up to 512, writes the segment bytes, and writes `nbytes/512 - 1` as a 2-byte value at offset 508.
Robustness requirement: the installed riscv64-linux-gnu-gcc emits extra non-PT_LOAD program headers (PHDR, INTERP, DYNAMIC, GNU_STACK, and zero-memsz ones) that make the naive reference implementation crash. Your implementation MUST: only write segments with p_type == PT_LOAD and p_memsz > 0, and copy via a fixed-size buffer loop (e.g. 512-byte chunks, zero-padding the final partial sector) rather than a variable-length array. Keep the printed output format consistent with the surrounding code.
Verify: cd /workspace/Project1-Bootloader && make CC=riscv64-linux-gnu-gcc must complete and produce ./image without crashing; then confirm with `xxd -s 508 -l 4 image` that a plausible non-zero sector count was written at offset 508, and that the image size is a multiple of 512.

1	# Project6: File System
2	
3	## 实验说明
4	### 开发环境
5	本实验用到的RISC-V开发板是XILINX PYNQ Z2开发板，开发板上有ARM核和FPGA，RISC-V核烧写到FPGA中。在开发板上电时由ARM核启动相关程序(BOOT.bin)，将RISC-V核烧入FPGA。之后，RISC-V核自动加载相关程序。RISC-V核为采用SiFive开源的Rocket核心。其基本信息为：
6	1. RV64IMAFDC(GC)指令集
7	2. 双核五级流水处理器
8	3. 数据/指令缓存大小各为16KB，4路组相联
9	4. 时钟频率为100MHz
10	
11	另外我们需要一张SD卡。将SD卡格式化为两个分区：第一个分区34MB，采用fat32文件系统；剩余空间全部划入第二个分区，保持第二个分区为空分区。制作完以后，将预先提供的BOOT.bin和RV_BOOT.bin拷入到第一个分区。
12	
13	### 运行方法
14	拿到裸开发板以后，需要将开发板按如下方式配置：
15	1. 将开发板设置为SD卡启动。PYNQ Z2支持从SD、QSPI和JTAG启动。我们将跳线插到最左侧，选择用SD卡启动。
16	2. 设置电源选项。PYNQ Z2支持电源供电和Micro-USB供电。我们把跳线插到USB这个选项上，用Micro-USB直接供电。
17	
18	配置完开发板后：
19	1. 将SD卡插入电脑中，将Makefile中的DISK的路径改为SD卡所在的路径。
20	2. 执行make all命令和make floppy命令，将内核镜像拷贝到SD卡中。
21	3. 将SD卡插入开发板中，使用Micro-USB线连接电脑和开发板。该线同时兼顾供电和传输数据的功能。
22	4. 打开开发板电源开关，开发板上会有红色和绿色的指示灯亮起，表明开发板已开始工作。
23	5. 使用minicom连接开发板，然后按下开发板的RESET按键。
24	6. 在minicom中出现bbl字样后，输入loadbootm以双核方式启动操作系统。
25	
26	---
27	## 内核部分说明
28	### 相关目录结构
29	| 文件夹 | 说明 |
30	| :--- | :--- |
31	| arch/riscv | 体系结构相关代码 |
32	| drivers | 驱动代码 |
33	| include | 头文件 |
34	| init | 初始化代码 |
35	| kernel | 内核主要文件 |
36	| libs | 内核使用的库 |
37	
38	### 文件系统
39	本操作系统的文件系统实现包括超级块、i-node bitmap、block bitmap、i-node、数据区，共有4096个i-node和1GB的数据区，数据区中一个block为4KB。在shell中文件系统相关的命令包括mkfs、statfs、mkdir、rmdir、ls、cd、touch、cat、ln。文件系统的主要文件在kernel/fs/中：disk.c中包括内存和磁盘的数据交换操作；fs.c中包括文件系统的基本操作；file.c中包括文件的相关操作。
40	
41	磁盘的布局请参考disk.h中的注释和宏定义。alloc_inode可以申请一个空闲的i-node并返回空闲i-node的id，如果返回0xffff则申请失败；free_inode可以将id为inode_id的i-node释放。alloc_block可以申请一个空闲的block并返回空闲block的id，如果返回0xffffffff则申请失败；free_block可以将id为block_id的block释放。disk.c中的read函数负责将相应的磁盘块读取到内存相应区域中，write函数负责将内存相应区域中的内容写到磁盘中。读写i-node和block时要提供相应的id，内存中缓存的i-node的id记录在cached_inode_id中，缓存的block的id记录在cached_block_id中。另外，因为一个扇区包括8个i-node，read_inode会返回i-node在内存中的地址。
42	
43	磁盘块对应的缓存信息、超级块、i-node、目录项的数据结构请参考fs.h。初始化文件系统的流程包括检查超级块的magic，清空block map和i-node map，设置根目录，设置超级块。mkdir，rmdir需要解析路径到倒数第二级目录，然后进行操作；ls，cd需要解析路径到最后一级目录。硬链接文件直接使用目标文件的i-node；软链接文件有单独的i-node，但是使用目标文件的block，此处与linux的做法略有不同，这一点造成删除软链接文件不会影响原文件，但删除原文件后使用软链接文件可能造成错误。
44	
45	文件描述的数据结构请参考file.h，文件描述使用内核中的全局数组，由所有的进程共用。do_touch函数先解析目录，然后申请i-node并修改倒数第二级目录。do_cat函数先解析目录，然后将文件第一个扇区的内容拷贝到buffer中。do_fopen函数先解析路径，然后申请并初始化文件描述。do_fread函数将文件的内容拷贝到buffer中，要注意间址块的情况。do_fwrite函数先申请需要的block，然后将buffer的内容写到文件中。do_fclose函数释放相应的文件描述。
46	
47	---
48	## 用户部分说明
49	### shell支持的命令
50	| 命令 | 参数 | 说明 |
51	| :---: | :---: | :--- |
52	| ps |  无 | 显示所有进程的pid，状态，MASK和运行在哪个核上 |
53	| reset | 无 | 清空下半屏（命令行） |
54	| clear | 无 | 清空上半屏（用户输出） |
55	| exec | name | 将名称为name的任务启动 |
56	| kill | pid | 杀死进程号为pid的进程 |
57	| taskset | -p mask pid | 设置进程号为pid的进程的MASK |
58	| mkfs | (-f) | （强制）初始化文件系统 | 
59	| statfs | 无 | 打印文件系统相关信息 |
60	| mkdir | path | 新建目录 | 
61	| rmdir | path | 删除目录 | 
62	| ls | -k或(-al) (path) | -k表示打印内核镜像中的可执行文件；否则打印目录中的所有内容，-al表示打印详细信息，不输入path表示当前目录 |  
63	| cd | path | 更改目录 | 
64	| touch | path | 新建文件 | 
65	| cat | path | 打印所选文件内容 | 
66	| ln |  (-s) source file | 将source(软)硬链接到file |
67	
68	注：MASK=1表示进程被允许运行在core 0；MASK=2表示进程被允许运行在core 1；MASK=3表示进程被允许运行在core 0和core 1。

payload.resultSummary:
Done. Everything verified.

## Files changed
- `/workspace/Project1-Bootloader/createimage.c` (only file touched)

## Functions implemented
- `write_segment` (`createimage.c:123`): skips any program header that isn't `PT_LOAD` or has `p_memsz == 0` (handles the PHDR/INTERP/DYNAMIC/GNU_STACK/zero-memsz headers riscv64-linux-gnu-gcc emits); rounds `p_memsz` up to a 512-byte boundary; copies the segment from `p_offset` in fixed 512-byte stack-buffer chunks (no VLA), zero-filling bss (`memsz > filesz`) and zero-padding the final partial sector; advances `*nbytes` by the padded byte count.
- `write_os_size` (`createimage.c:171`): writes `nbytes/512 - 1` as a 2-byte little-endian value at image offset 508 and prints `os_size: N sectors`, matching the reference idiom.

## Build & verification
- Command: `cd /workspace/Project1-Bootloader && make CC=riscv64-linux-gnu-gcc` (Makefile variable is `CC`, not `CROSS_PREFIX`; host tool builds with `gcc`).
- Result: clean build, no warnings from `createimage.c`; `./createimage --extended bootblock kernel` ran without crashing (previously it would hit a zero-memsz segment), printed the expected `--extended` segment listing, and produced `./image`.
- Checks: image size is 1024 bytes (multiple of 512); `od -j 508 -N 4 image` shows `01 00 00 00` — sector count 1 = 1024/512 − 1, correct. `xxd` isn't installed, so `od` was used instead. The kernel's `filesz 0x19c / memsz 0x1d8` segment also exercised the bss zero-padding path.
- Build artifacts (`image`, `createimage`, etc.) left in place as instructed.

## Assumptions/concerns
- `nbytes` is an `int` count of image bytes; with the bootblock at 1 sector, `os_size = total_sectors - 1` matches what the bootblock expects to read at offset 508. No concerns remaining.

payload.resultSummary:
Done. All stubs in my two assigned files are implemented and the project compiles.

**Files changed** (only these two):
- `/workspace/Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part1/kernel/sched/sched.c`
- `/workspace/Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part1/kernel/locking/lock.c`

**Functions implemented:**
- `do_scheduler()` — cooperative round-robin: if the current task is still `TASK_RUNNING`, mark it `TASK_READY` and re-queue it at the head of `ready_queue`; dequeue `ready_queue.next` as the new `current_running` (via `list_entry(..., pcb_t, list)`), mark it `TASK_RUNNING`, update global `process_id`, restore the task's VT100 cursor (`vt100_move_cursor` + `screen_cursor_x/y`), then `switch_to(prev_running, current_running)`. Single-CPU design — this project has no `get_current_cpu_id()` anywhere, so plain `current_running` is used, matching `init/main.c` and `futex.c`.
- `do_block(pcb_node, queue)` — `list_del` the node, `list_add` it onto the given block queue, set the pcb status to `TASK_BLOCKED`.
- `do_unblock(pcb_node)` — `list_del` the node, `list_add` it onto `ready_queue`, set status `TASK_READY`.
- `do_mutex_lock_acquire(lock)` — while `lock->lock.status == LOCKED`, `do_block(&current_running->list, &lock->block_queue)` then `do_scheduler()`; after waking and re-checking, set status to `LOCKED`.
- `do_mutex_lock_release(lock)` — set status `UNLOCKED`, then if the lock's block queue is non-empty, `do_unblock(lock->block_queue.next)` (wakes exactly one waiter, which then owns the lock).

**Design verification:** `kernel.txt` in this directory is a leftover disassembly of a reference build; I matched my implementations against the disassembled `do_scheduler`, `do_block`, `do_unblock`, `do_mutex_lock_acquire`, and `do_mutex_lock_release` (instruction-for-instruction equivalence: same list ops at head via `list_add`, same status values, single-waiter wakeup in release). Callers in `kernel/locking/futex.c`, `init/main.c`, and `test/test_project2/test_lock*.c` all use these exact signatures/semantics.

**Build:** `cd /workspace/Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part1 && make CROSS_PREFIX=riscv64-linux-gnu- main` — exit 0, zero errors (only pre-existing warnings from `tiny_libc` and an RWX-segment linker warning), `main` ELF (84 KB) produced. The known `createimage` segfault issue was not encountered since only the `main` target was built.

**Assumptions/notes:** `do_block`/`do_unblock` use `list_add` (head insert) rather than `list_add_tail` — this matches both the reference disassembly and the head-insert convention used by `init_pcb()` for `ready_queue`. Build artifacts were left in place per instructions.

payload.resultSummary:
Done. All stubs in my five assigned files are implemented and the project compiles.

## Files changed (all under `/workspace/Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part2/`)

- `kernel/sched/sched.c`
- `kernel/sched/time.c`
- `kernel/locking/lock.c`
- `kernel/locking/binsem.c`
- `kernel/locking/futex.c`

## Functions implemented

The repo's `kernel.txt` disassembly was generated from the original (pre-stub) build, so I decoded it to recover the exact reference semantics for each function:

- `scheduler()` (sched.c) — saves current task's cursor; if current is still `TASK_RUNNING`, re-queues it at the tail of `ready_queue`, sets `TASK_READY`, stamps `ready_tick`; switches `current_running` to `max_priority_node()`'s pcb (list_del, `TASK_RUNNING`, update `process_id`); restores the new task's cursor via `vt100_move_cursor` + `screen_cursor_x/y`; wraps everything in `test_sched_time(BEGIN/END)`. No register save/restore — that is done by `do_scheduler`/`ret_from_exception` in entry.S.
- `max_priority_node()` (sched.c) — scans `ready_queue`; effective priority = `priority − (get_ticks() − ready_tick) / timer_interval` (lower value wins, aging prevents starvation); strictly-less comparison so ties keep the earlier-queued node; returns the first node if only one.
- `timer_check()` (time.c) — under `disable_preempt()`, walks `timer_queue`; for each timer with `get_ticks() >= timeout_tick`, invokes `callback_func(parameter)` then removes the node (`node = node->next; list_del(node->prev)` idiom); ends with `enable_preempt()`.
- `do_mutex_lock_acquire()` (lock.c) — while the lock is `LOCKED`, `do_block` current task on `lock->block_queue` and `do_scheduler()`; sets `LOCKED` on exit.
- `do_mutex_lock_release()` (lock.c) — sets `UNLOCKED`; if block queue non-empty, `do_unblock` the first waiter and `do_scheduler()`.
- `binsem_op()` (binsem.c) — under preempt-off: `BINSEM_OP_LOCK` decrements `sem`, blocks current task + reschedules if `sem < 0`; `BINSEM_OP_UNLOCK` increments `sem`, unblocks one waiter + reschedules if `sem <= 0`.
- `get_node()` (futex.c, static) — hashes `val_addr` via `futex_hash`, scans the bucket for a matching `futex_key`; if missing and `create`, `kmalloc(sizeof(futex_node_t))`, set key, `init_list_head(&block_queue)`, `list_add_tail` into the bucket; else NULL.
- `futex_wait()` (futex.c) — preempt-off; `get_node(addr, 1)` + `assert(node)`; if `*val_addr == val`, `do_block` on the node's queue and `scheduler()`; preempt-on.
- `futex_wakeup()` (futex.c) — preempt-off; `get_node(addr, 0)`; if found, unblocks up to `num_wakeup` waiters (stop at empty queue); calls `scheduler()` unconditionally (matches reference); preempt-on.

## Build verification

`cd /workspace/Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part2 && make CROSS_PREFIX=riscv64-linux-gnu- main` — compiles and links cleanly (`main` ELF produced). Only pre-existing warnings remain (tiny_libc `stdatomic.h` void*-deref, RWX LOAD segment); no warnings or errors from my files. I did not run the full `make` (createimage step), per the known toolchain issue.

## Assumptions / notes

- Priority semantics: lower `priority` value = higher priority, with wait-time aging subtracted — taken directly from the reference disassembly of `max_priority_node` in `kernel.txt`.
- `futex_wakeup` calls `scheduler()` even when no node/waiters exist; this mirrors the reference build (the `beqz` jumps to the `scheduler` call site).
- Signatures, globals, and all non-stub code untouched; no other files modified.

payload.resultSummary:
All done — net.c is warning-free, no stubs remain, and the kernel links. Final summary:

## Files changed
- `/workspace/Project5-Device_Driver/drivers/net.c` (the only file modified)

## Functions implemented
The design mirrors the fully-implemented `net.c` in the Project6 snapshot (same course codebase, one project later), adapted to P5's API (P5 has no `get_kva_of`; user addresses are accessed directly under the SUM bit, exactly as P5's pre-filled `XEmacPsRecvHandler` in `drivers/emacps/xemacps_main.c` expects):

- `do_net_recv(addr, length, num_packet, frLength)` — rejects `num_packet > RXBD_CNT` (-1); sets `recv_transaction = 1`, enables SUM, zeroes `rx_buffers[]`/`rx_len[]`, and programs the RX BDs via `EmacPsRecv(&EmacPsInstance, 0, num_packet)` (BDs were pre-bound to `rx_buffers[]` in `EmacPsSetupBD`). Poll mode (`net_poll_mode == 0`): busy-waits with `EmacPsWaitRecv`, copies each frame out of `rx_buffers[i]` to the user buffer, records lengths into `frLength[]` (using the `rx_curr`/`rx_tail` globals), disables SUM, clears `recv_transaction`, returns total bytes received. IRQ mode (`== 1`): stashes `addr`/`num_packet`/`frLength` into the `_addr`/`_num_packet`/`_frLength` globals that `XEmacPsRecvHandler` consumes, blocks on `net_recv_queue` with `do_block(...); scheduler();` (P5's established idiom — the pre-filled handler copies the frames and calls `do_unblock(net_recv_queue.next)`), then disables SUM and returns 0.
- `do_net_send(addr, length)` — sets `send_transaction = 1`, enables SUM, clears `tx_buffer`, memcpy's the user packet into it, starts DMA via `EmacPsSend`. Poll mode: `EmacPsWaitSend` then clears `send_transaction`; IRQ mode: blocks on `net_send_queue` (`do_block` + `scheduler()`) until `XEmacPsSendHandler` unblocks it. Disables SUM on exit.
- `do_net_irq_mode(mode)` — on a real mode change (asserting no send/recv transaction is in flight), stores `net_poll_mode = mode`; mode 1 (IRQ) enables the NIC's TX/RX/error interrupt bits via `XEmacPs_IntEnable(... - Return convention follows the Project6 reference and the test programs: poll mode returns total bytes received, IRQ mode returns 0, invalid `num_packet`/mode returns -1 (`test/recv.c` only prints the value).

## Files changed (all under `/workspace/Project3-Interactive_OS_and_Process_Management/`)

**`kernel/sched/sched.c`** — 6 stubs:

- `max_priority_node()` — scans `ready_queue` for the highest-`priority` task whose `mask` allows the current core (`mask & (1 << cpu_id)`); ties broken by smallest `ready_tick` (FIFO/round-robin among equal priorities, matching how `do_unblock`/`scheduler` stamp `ready_tick`).
- `do_spawn()` — finds a free pcb slot (`pid == -1`, returns -1 if none), allocates 1-page kernel + user stacks via `allocPage(1)` (matches the reaper's `freePage(base, 1)` in `init/main.c`), initializes all pcb fields (`pid = process_id++`, `mask = 3`, `mode`, `priority` from `task_info_t`, wait_list, binsem count), builds the initial `regs_context_t` on the kernel stack exactly like `init_pcb_stack` in `init/main.c` (`ra`/`sepc` = entry, `sp` = user stack, `gp` = `__global_pointer$`, `sstatus = SR_SPIE`, `sscratch` = pcb) plus `a0 = arg`, and enqueues to `ready_queue`.
- `do_exit()` — releases held binsems (via a new `static` helper `release_binsems()` that does sem++ and transfers ownership to the first blocked waiter, mirroring the unlock path), frees the user stack, wakes every task on its `wait_list`, then either becomes `TASK_ZOMBIE` (`ENTER_ZOMBIE_ON_EXIT`, reaped later by `do_waitpid`) or is appended to `kernel_pcb[0].wait_list` (`AUTO_CLEANUP_ON_EXIT`, reaped by the pre-existing cleanup loop in `main()`), and reschedules.
- `do_kill(pid)` — returns 0 if no such pid; otherwise removes the victim from whatever queue it's in (`list_del` is a safe no-op for running tasks), releases its binsems, frees its user stack, wakes its waiters, marks it ZOMBIE or queues it for kernel cleanup per its mode, reschedules if it killed itself, returns 1.
- `do_waitpid(pid, ...)` — returns 0 if pid not found; blocks the caller on the target's `wait_list` until the target is ZOMBIE/EXITED, then the first woken waiter reaps a zombie (status → EXITED, `pid = -1`, frees kernel stack); returns the pid.

**`kernel/locking/binsem.c`** — 1 stub:
- `binsem_op()` — `BINSEM_OP_LOCK`: sem--, block on the node's `block_queue` if contended, else record the id in the pcb's `binsem_id[]`/`binsem_num` (so `do_exit`/`do_kill` can release it). `BINSEM_OP_UNLOCK`: sem++, drop one held record, and if waiters exist hand ownership to the first one and unblock it. Wrapped in `disable_preempt`/`enable_preempt` per the futex idiom.

**`kernel/syscall/mailbox.c`** — 3 stubs (design taken from the intact Project4 snapshot, adapted to P3's `k`-prefixed string API and no-SUM environment):
- `do_mbox_open()` — returns the id of an existing same-named mailbox (bumping `opned`), else allocates the next `mailbox_t` slot and a free `message_status[]` slot, initializes name/wait_queue/buffer, returns id.
- `do_mbox_send()` — if the message wouldn't fit in the `MAX_MBOX_LENGTH` circular buffer, blocks on the mailbox `wait_queue` and returns 0 (user library retries); else appends bytes, wakes all blocked waiters, reschedules, returns 1.
- `do_mbox_recv()` — symmetric: blocks + returns 0 when not enough data; otherwise consumes from the buffer tail, wakes blocked senders, reschedules, returns 1.

`cd /workspace/Project3-Interactive_OS_and_Process_Management && make CROSS_PREFIX=riscv64-linux-gnu- main` — compiles and links cleanly; the only diagnostics are pre-existing warnings in untouched files (`tiny_libc/include/stdatomic.h` void-pointer dereferences, RWX LOAD segment). All done. Final report:

## Files changed (only the 3 assigned files)

**`/workspace/Project6-File_System/kernel/fs/disk.c`** (4 stubs):
- `alloc_inode()` — reads inode map into `INODEMAP_CACHE`, scans the 512 bytes for the first non-`0xff` byte, sets the lowest free bit, writes the map back, increments `superblock->used_inode_num`, returns the inode id (`0xffff` if full).
- `alloc_block()` — same over the 64-sector block map (64*512 bytes), returns block id (`0xffffffff` if full), updates `used_block_num`.
- `free_inode(uint16_t)` — clears bit `inode_id % 8` of byte `inode_id / 8` in the inode map, flushes with `write_inodemap()`, decrements `used_inode_num`, flushes superblock.
- `free_block(uint32_t)` — same for the block map via `write_blockmap()`.

**`/workspace/Project6-File_System/kernel/fs/fs.c`** (6 stubs):
- `mkfs(int print)` — returns 0 if magic already matches (restoring `current_dir_inode/block` from the superblock); otherwise clears both bitmaps, allocates root inode+block, builds the root `dir_t` with `.`/`..`, fills all superblock fields (layout constants from `disk.h`), writes everything to disk, returns 1. Prints exactly 11 progress lines when `print` is set (matching `do_mkfs`'s `*print_location_y += 11`).
- `do_mkdir` — parses the path (absolute from root if leading `/`, else from cwd) to the parent directory, rejects duplicates, then takes a free dentry, allocates inode+block, bumps parent link count, initializes the new dir with `.`/`..`.
- `do_rmdir` — same path resolution; refuses non-empty dirs (anything besides `.`/`..`), then clears the dentry, decrements parent link, frees block (when `inode->mode == 0`) and inode.
- `do_ls` — resolves the path to the final directory; mode 0 prints names (`prints("%s    ")` + newline, advances `*print_location_y` by 1); mode 1 prints `name/type/owner/size/link` per entry and advances by the entry count. Returns 1 on success, 0 if the path doesn't resolve.
- `do_cd` — resolves the full path (so `.` and `..` work via the dir entries) and updates `current_dir_inode`/`current_dir_block`.
- `do_link` — resolves the source to its inode; mode 0 (hard link): rejects dirs, `link++`, adds a `FILE` dentry in cwd pointing at the same inode; mode 1 (soft link): allocates a new inode (`mode = 1`) that shares the target's direct/indirect block pointers, per the README's design.

**`/workspace/Project6-File_System/kernel/fs/file.c`** (5 stubs):
- `do_touch` — resolves parent dir, rejects duplicate `FILE` names, adds a `FILE` dentry with a fresh inode (`size = 0`, `link = 1`, owner = current pid).
- `do_cat` — resolves the file, zeroes `buffer` (`size + 1`), copies the first data block (up to 4096 bytes, per README) into it.
- `do_fopen` — resolves the file, takes a free slot in the global `fd_list[10]`, records inode/access and zeroes `rd_pos`/`wr_pos`; returns the fd, `-1` if the file is missing or no slot is free.
- `do_fread` — rejects `O_WRONLY` fds and reads past EOF; walks direct blocks then the two single-indirect blocks, copying 4KB-block-wise through `BLOCK_CACHE`, advancing `rd_pos`; returns `size`.
- `do_fwrite` — rejects `O_RDONLY`; grows `inode->size`, allocates newly needed blocks (allocating indirect pointer blocks when crossing the 10 / 10+1024 thresholds), flushes the inode, then writes block-wise through `BLOCK_CACHE` honoring `wr_pos` (partial blocks handled by read-modify-write of the cached 4KB block); returns `size`.

All path-parsing follows the file-local idiom: `enable_sum()` around user-pointer access, root-vs-cwd start, 128-entry `dir_t` scans, `read_inode`/`read_block` cache wrappers.

## Deviations from the upstream reference (bug fixes only)
- `free_inode`/`free_block`: the upstream original cleared the lowest *set* bit and wrote it back to byte `id % 8` (wrong byte); I clear exactly bit `id % 8` of byte `id / 8`.
- `do_link` soft link: upstream copied block pointers with index `i` instead of `j` inside the `j` loop (out-of-bounds); fixed to `j`. Also added a source-not-found guard, a missing `disable_sum()`, and a final `return 0`.
- `do_rmdir`: captures `inode->mode` into a local before later `read_inode()` calls clobber `INODE_CACHE`.
- `do_cat`/`do_fopen`: guards for file-not-found / fd-table-full (`return 0` / `-1`) instead of using an uninitialized pointer or writing past `fd_list[10]`.

## Build
- `make CROSS_PREFIX=riscv64-linux-gnu- main` — my files compile cleanly (only benign signedness/`volatile`-cast warnings, same as upstream style).
- Two pre-existing, unrelated build issues: (1) prebuilt host tools `elf2char`/`generateMapping` lacked the execute bit — fixed with `chmod +x` (no content change); (2) final link fails under GCC 13's default `-fno-common` because the *generated* `include/user_programs.h` + `kernel/user_programs.c` define `int _length_...` in multiple TUs — pre-existing toolchain issue in generated files, worked around by adding `-fcommon` via a command-line `CFLAGS` override (no repo files modified). payload.resultSummary:
All 15 stubs in my two assigned files are implemented and the kernel links. Final report:

## Files changed (only these two)

`/workspace/Project6-File_System/kernel/mm/mm.c` — 9 stubs:

- `alloc_user_page(pin, pgtable)` — first-fit over `user_page[]`; on exhaustion picks a victim via `selete_page()`, evicts it with `write_to_sd()`, then reuses the slot; records `pin` and the owner's leaf PTE pointer.
- `selete_page()` — NRU/second-chance: first pass returns a valid, unpinned page whose PTE `_PAGE_ACCESSED` is clear (clearing the bit on pages it skips), second pass takes any valid unpinned page; asserts if none.
- `write_to_sd(pa)` — allocates a free `disk_page[]` swap slot, writes the page with `sbi_sd_write` (8 sectors at `SWAP_BEGIN + slot*8`), clears `_PAGE_PRESENT` on the owner PTE, stores the slot id in the PTE pfn field, sets `_PAGE_SOFT`, frees the `user_page[]` entry, flushes TLB.
- `init_page_table()` — allocates a pgdir page, copies the shared kernel mapping entry (VPN2 0x101, 2MB large pages) from `PGDIR_PA`, then builds the 3-level SV39 walk for `USER_STACK_ADDR - PAGE_SIZE` and maps a freshly allocated pinned user-stack page (P|R|W|X|U|A|D).
- `free_process_user_page(pgdir)` — walks all 3 levels (skipping shared VPN2 0x101), frees leaf pages (shared-memory pages decrement `shm_page[]` count and are only freed at 0), frees swap slots of `_PAGE_SOFT` PTEs, and releases all page-table pages + pgdir via `free_pgdir_page`.
- `alloc_page_helper(va, pgdir)` — builds missing second/last-level tables on demand, maps a freshly allocated unpinned user page at the leaf (P|R|W|X|U|A|D), returns `get_kva_of(va, pgdir)` (used by `load_elf`).
- `shm_page_get(key)` — allocates the shared physical page on first use (pinned, zeroed), bumps the refcount, maps it into the current pgdir at `0x1000 + key*PAGE_SIZE` (the documented share region), returns that va.
- `shm_page_dt(addr)` — clears the leaf PTE in the current pgdir, decrements the refcount, frees the physical page at 0.
- `handle_page_fault(regs, stval, cause)` — walks the current pgdir; unmapped levels/leaves → demand paging via `alloc_page_helper` (needed by `test_large` touching va 0x20000); `_PAGE_SOFT` leaf → allocates a page, `sbi_sd_read`s the swap slot back, frees the disk slot, restores full attributes and `_PAGE_PRESENT`.

`/workspace/Project6-File_System/kernel/sched/sched.c` — 6 stubs:

- `scheduler()` — requeues current if still `TASK_RUNNING` (updating `ready_tick`), picks via `max_priority_node()`, sets `RUNNING`/`cpu_id`/`current_running[cpu_id]`/`current_cpu_running`, switches `satp` to the task's pgdir and flushes the TLB.
- `max_priority_node()` — scans `ready_queue`, mask-filtered (`mask & (1<<cpu_id)`), highest `priority` wins, ties broken by earliest `ready_tick`.
- `do_exec(...)` — finds a free pcb (0 = too many tasks), looks up the ELF via `get_elf_file` (-1 = not found), replicates `init_pcb`'s pcb layout (kernel stack page, own pgdir from `init_page_table`, inherited hart mask), loads the ELF with `load_elf`/`alloc_page_helper` (-2 with full rollback on bad ELF), pushes argv strings + pointer array onto the new user stack via its kernel mapping (SUM enabled for reading caller's user memory), and sets up the trap frame (a0=argc, a1=argv va, sp/sepc/ra/sstatus=`SR_SPIE`, sscratch=pcb). Return codes match `test_shell.c`'s expectations.
- `do_exit()` — releases all held binsems (unblocking one waiter each, mirroring `binsem_op`), wakes everything on its `wait_list`, becomes `TASK_ZOMBIE`; for `AUTO_CLEANUP_ON_EXIT` also frees the address space and queues the pcb on `kernel_pcb[0].wait_list` (the main-loop reaper frees the kernel stack); then reschedules.
- `do_kill(pid)` — returns 0 if no such pid; self-kill defers to `do_exit()`; otherwise releases binsems, wakes waiters, frees the address space (guarded by `pgdir != NULL` so a zombie's pages are freed exactly once), pulls it out of its queue (NULL-safe `list_del`), and hands it to the cleanup list.
- `do_waitpid(pid, ...)` — returns 0 if no such pid; blocks the caller on the target's `wait_list` until `TASK_ZOMBIE`, then frees the target's VM resources (pgdir-guarded) and queues the pcb for reaping (only for `ENTER_ZOMBIE_ON_EXIT`, avoiding double-queueing of auto-cleaned tasks).

## Build

- `make CROSS_PREFIX=riscv64-linux-gnu- main`: my files compile cleanly (warnings only); the final link fails on `multiple definition of _length___test_*_elf` — a **pre-existing** issue: the pre-filled `elf2char` emits non-`extern` definitions into the generated `include/user_programs.h`, and GCC 13 defaults to `-fno-common`. Not caused by, and not fixable within, my assigned files.
- Verified end-to-end with a flag-only override (no files touched): `make CROSS_PREFIX=riscv64-linux-gnu- CFLAGS="... -fcommon" main` → links, `main` produced (470 KB). Standalone `-c` compiles of `mm.c` and `sched.c` with the stock flags also pass (warnings only; the `prints` implicit-declaration warnings in `do_show_exec`/`fs.c` are pre-existing).

## Assumptions / concerns

- `user_page_t.pgtable` is used as the **leaf PTE pointer (kva)** of the owning mapping — this is what makes NRU accessed-bit checks and swap-out PTE invalidation possible; kernel stacks and shm pages pass NULL and are pinned, so they're never victims.
- Swap slot ids are stored in the PTE pfn field with `_PAGE_SOFT` set (DISK_PAGE_NUM=256 fits), standard for this course design.
- Killing a process RUNNING on the other core frees its pages underneath it — a known race in this course design (kernel lock doesn't cover user-mode execution); handled as in standard solutions.
- Artifacts (`main`, generated `user_programs.*`, `*.o`, tools) left in place per instructions.

All stubs in both assigned files are implemented and the Project4 kernel builds cleanly.

## Files changed (only the two assigned files)

**`/workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/kernel/mm/mm.c`**
- `alloc_user_page(pin, pgtable)` — scans the `user_page[]` pool for a free frame; if exhausted, evicts one via `selete_page()` + `write_to_sd()` and reuses that slot; records `valid/pin/pgtable` (the owner's leaf PTE) and returns the pa.
- `selete_page()` — NRU clock algorithm with a static clock hand: skips invalid/pinned pages and pages with no owner PTE; gives pages with `_PAGE_ACCESSED` a second chance by clearing the bit; returns the pa of the first unaccessed victim.
- `write_to_sd(pa)` — allocates a `disk_page[]` swap slot, writes the 4K page with `sbi_sd_write(pa, 8, SWAP_BEGIN + slot*8)`, then marks the owner's PTE swapped (clear `_PAGE_PRESENT`, set `_PAGE_SOFT`, disk slot stored in the pfn field), frees the frame, flushes TLB.
- `init_page_table()` — allocates a fresh pgdir from the pgdir pool, copies the kernel pgdir's `0x101` entry so the kernel large-page mapping is shared by every process (this is what lets the kernel run under a user satp), and pre-allocates/maps the user code region `0x10000–0x13000` (U|R|W|X) so `load_elf(..., get_kva_of)` in `main.c`/`do_exec` can copy segments.
- `free_process_user_page(pgdir)` — recursively walks the 3 levels, skipping the shared kernel entry `0x101`; frees swap slots for `_PAGE_SOFT` entries, decrements shm counts for va in `[0x1000,0x10000)` (frees the shm frame at count 0), frees all other mapped user frames, then frees the intermediate and root pgdir pages.
- `shm_page_get(key)` — maps va `0x1000 + key*PAGE_SIZE`: allocates a pinned physical page on first use (`shm_page[key].count == 0`), bumps the refcount, sets the leaf PTE (U|R|W), flushes TLB, returns the va.
- `shm_page_dt(addr)` — clears the caller's leaf PTE for the shm va, decrements the refcount, frees the frame when it reaches 0.
- `handle_page_fault(regs, stval, cause)` — guards kernel-va faults to `handle_other`; walks/creates the 3-level table for the faulting va; if the leaf is `_PAGE_SOFT` it allocates a frame and swaps the page back in with `sbi_sd_read`, freeing the disk slot; otherwise demand-allocates a zeroed frame; sets U|R|W|X|A|D, flushes TLB, and returns without advancing `sepc` so the faulting instruction retries.
- Added a `static PTE *get_leaf_pte(va, pgdir, alloc)` walk/create helper used by the above.

**`/workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/kernel/sched/sched.c`**
- `scheduler()` — picks `max_priority_node()`; if none can run on this core, keeps the current task; otherwise requeues the current task (if still `TASK_RUNNING`, refreshing `ready_tick`), dequeues the next, sets `current_running[cpu_id]` and `current_cpu_running` (the `$tp` trick in `ret_from_exception`), and switches address space with `set_satp(SATP_MODE_SV39, 0, pgdir>>12)` + TLB flush.
- `do_exec(file_name, argc, argv, mode)` — finds a free pcb (returns 0 if none), reads the embedded ELF via `get_elf_file` (returns -1 if missing) with `enable_sum()` while copying argv strings out of the caller's address space; mirrors `init_pcb()`/`init_pcb_stack()` from `main.c` (pinned kernel stack page, `init_page_table()`, `load_elf(..., get_kva_of)`); allocates and maps one user-stack page, pushes argv strings + pointer array onto it (16-byte aligned sp), and seeds `a0=argc, a1=argv, ra/sepc=entry, sstatus=SR_SPIE, sscratch=pcb`. Returns the new pid.
- `do_exit()` — releases held binsems (via a `release_binsem` helper that wakes blocked waiters), frees the whole address space with `free_process_user_page`, wakes waitpid waiters, then either becomes `TASK_ZOMBIE` (`ENTER_ZOMBIE_ON_EXIT`) or marks `TASK_EXITED` and hands the pcb to the reaper list `kernel_pcb[0].wait_list` that `main()` drains (the reaper frees the kernel stack we are still running on); ends with `scheduler()`.
- `do_kill(pid)` — refuses pid ≤ 1; self-kill delegates to `do_exit()`; otherwise removes the target from its queue, releases binsems, frees the address space and kernel stack, wakes its waiters, marks it `TASK_EXITED`/`pid=-1`. Returns 1/0.
- `do_waitpid(pid, ...)` — loops: returns -1 if no such pcb, reaps a `TASK_ZOMBIE` (frees kernel stack, resets pcb, returns pid), returns pid for `TASK_EXITED`, otherwise blocks on the target's `wait_list` and reschedules.
- `max_priority_node()` — scans `ready_queue` for the highest-priority task whose `mask` allows the current core, breaking ties by earliest `ready_tick` (FCFS).
- Added a `static PTE *walk_pgtable(va, pgdir)` helper (sched.c-local duplicate of the mm.c walker, since `get_leaf_pte` is static to mm.c and `mm.h` is not mine to change).

## Build

## Assumptions / concerns

- Swap layout: sector `SWAP_BEGIN (2048) + slot*8`, one page = 8 sectors, matching the `dd count=4096` image padding and `DISK_PAGE_NUM=256`.
- Shm va range follows the layout comment in mm.c (`0x1000–0x10000`); shm frames are pinned so NRU never evicts a frame shared by multiple address spaces.
- `scheduler()` updates `current_cpu_running` as well as `current_running[cpu_id]`, because `ret_from_exception` switches via `current_cpu_running` (set at trap entry in `interrupt_helper`).
- `do_kill` of a task currently running on the *other* core frees its page table out from under it — a known limitation of this design (no remote kill handshake); course tests kill ready/blocked/self tasks.
- Zombies wait for `do_waitpid` to free the kernel stack; auto-cleanup tasks are reaped by the existing `main()` loop, which only frees the kernel stack — hence `do_exit` must (and does) free the page table itself before scheduling away.

All 15 stubs in my two assigned files are implemented and the kernel links cleanly. Final report:

## Files changed (only these two)

**`/workspace/Project5-Device_Driver/kernel/mm/mm.c`** — 9 stubs:
- `alloc_user_page(pin, pgtable)` — first-fit over the `user_page[]` pool; on exhaustion evicts a victim via `selete_page()` + `write_to_sd()`; records valid/pin/owner-PTE, returns pa.
- `selete_page()` — NRU/second-chance: first pass picks a valid unpinned page whose PTE A-bit is 0 (clearing A on pages it skips); second pass takes the first valid unpinned page; asserts if all pinned.
- `write_to_sd(pa)` — grabs a free `disk_page[]` slot, `sbi_sd_write`s the page (8 × 512B blocks at `SWAP_BEGIN + slot*8`), then marks the owner's PTE as swapped (clear `_PAGE_PRESENT`, set `_PAGE_SOFT`, swap-slot index stored in the pfn field), frees the user page, flushes TLB.
- `init_page_table()` — allocates a fresh pgdir, copies boot-pgdir entries `0x001` (identity map) and `0x101` (kernel large-page map) so kernel/trap code is reachable under every process satp, eagerly maps one user-stack page at `USER_STACK_ADDR - PAGE_SIZE`, returns pgdir pa.
- `free_process_user_page(pgdir)` — walks all 3 SV39 levels (skipping shared kernel entries 0x001/0x101), frees mapped user pages (decrementing shm refcounts, freeing only at 0), releases swap slots of `_PAGE_SOFT` entries, frees intermediate page-table pages via `free_pgdir_page`, flushes TLB.
- `alloc_page_helper(va, pgdir)` — 3-level walk allocating missing intermediate tables (`alloc_pgdir_page`) and, if the leaf is absent, a user page mapped `PRESENT|R|W|X|U|A|D`; returns kva (used by `load_elf` in pre-filled `init_pcb`).
- `shm_page_get(key)` — index `key % SHM_PAGE_NUM`, va = `0x1000 + key*PAGE_SIZE` (share area); first caller gets a pinned zeroed page, others bump the refcount; maps it U/RW into the caller's pgdir, returns va.
- `shm_page_dt(addr)` — locates the caller's PTE, decrements the shm refcount (frees page at 0), unmaps the page, flushes TLB.
- `handle_page_fault(regs, stval, cause)` — if the leaf PTE has `_PAGE_SOFT`: swap-in (alloc page, `sbi_sd_read` the slot, free slot, restore PRESENT/A); if never mapped: demand-allocate via `alloc_page_helper` (also gives stack growth); flush TLB and retry the faulting instruction. Added two file-local helpers `walk_pgdir`/`walk_pgdir_alloc`.

**`/workspace/Project5-Device_Driver/kernel/sched/sched.c`** — 6 stubs:
- `scheduler()` — requeues the current process if still `TASK_RUNNING` (kernel idle pcbs, pid 0, are never queued), picks via `max_priority_node()` (falls back to `kernel_pcb[cpu_id]` when no candidate), updates `current_running`/`current_cpu_running`, and switches satp to the next process's pgdir + TLB flush.
- `max_priority_node()` — scans `ready_queue`, skipping dead (`pgdir == NULL`) and wrong-hart (`mask`) entries; highest `priority` wins, ties broken by earliest `ready_tick` (FIFO as all priorities are 0).
- `do_exec(file_name, argc, argv, mode)` — `enable_sum` (args live in caller space); finds elf via `get_elf_file` (−1 if missing), free pcb slot (0 if none); allocates pinned kernel stack, `init_page_table()`, `load_elf` with `alloc_page_helper`; copies argv strings + pointer array onto the new user stack; builds the trap frame (ra/sepc=entry, sp, gp=`__global_pointer$`, a0/a1=argc/argv, `SR_SPIE`, sscratch=pcb) exactly like `init_pcb_stack` in `init/main.c`; enqueues READY, returns new pid.
- `do_exit()` — releases held binsems (waking blocked peers, mirroring `binsem_op` unlock), wakes waiters on `wait_list`; `ENTER_ZOMBIE_ON_EXIT` → `TASK_ZOMBIE` (VM freed later by `do_waitpid`); `AUTO_CLEANUP_ON_EXIT` → frees VM + pgdir immediately and hands pcb/kernel-stack to the core-0 reaper list (`kernel_pcb[0].wait_list`, matching pre-filled `main()`); then `scheduler()`.
- `do_kill(pid)` — self-kill delegates to `do_exit`; otherwise validates target (not zombie/exited), releases its binsems, wakes waiters, removes it from its queue, frees VM + pgdir, marks zombie, and puts it on the reaper list. Returns 1/0.
- `do_waitpid(pid, ...)` — finds target (0 if unknown/exited); blocks the caller on the target's `wait_list` until it zombifies; then reaps: frees VM + pgdir (guarded by `pgdir != NULL` so auto-cleaned processes aren't double-freed or double-queued), moves pcb to the reaper list, returns pid.

## Build verification
- `make CROSS_PREFIX=riscv64-linux-gnu- main` — my files compile warning-free; the final link initially failed on `multiple definition of _length___test_*_elf`, a **pre-existing** incompatibility: the pre-filled `elf2char --header-only` emits non-`extern` tentative definitions in the generated header, which GCC ≥ 10 (`-fno-common` default) rejects — same class of pre-filled-toolchain issue as the known `createimage` segfault, not caused by my changes.
- Verified two ways: (1) both files compile standalone with the exact Makefile flags — clean, zero warnings; (2) full link with `make CROSS_PREFIX=riscv64-linux-gnu- CC="riscv64-linux-gnu-gcc -fcommon" main` — **succeeds**, producing `main` (only the benign `LOAD segment with RWX permissions` ld warning). I did not modify any pre-filled file to achieve this; I only `chmod +x`'d the prebuilt host tools (`elf2char`, `createimage`, `generateMapping`) which shipped without execute permission. Build artifacts (`main`, generated `include/user_programs.h`, `kernel/user_programs.c`) left in place per instructions.

## Assumptions / concerns
- Swap protocol is my design (documented by the bookkeeping structs): PTE `_PAGE_SOFT` + slot-in-pfn marks swapped pages; swap slots are 8 SD blocks from `SWAP_BEGIN`.
- `do_exec` return codes follow `test/test_shell.c`: `-1` no such program, `0` no free pcb; `-2` ("memory full") is never returned because the allocators assert instead of failing.
- Killing a process that is mid-`do_sleep` leaves a pending timer whose `do_unblock` would requeue it; `max_priority_node`'s `pgdir == NULL` skip makes this harmless. Killing a process running on the *other* hart is not specially handled (standard for this codebase; kills in tests target ready/blocked tasks).
- Shm va is `0x1000 + key*PAGE_SIZE` per the layout comment; `SHMP_KEY 0x42` in `test/echo.c` fits `SHM_PAGE_NUM` directly.

args.description: Review implemented OS subsystems for bugs
items:
PROJECT: /workspace/Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part1. FILES TO REVIEW (only these may be modified): kernel/sched/sched.c (do_scheduler, do_block, do_unblock) and kernel/locking/lock.c (do_mutex_lock_acquire, do_mutex_lock_release).
Focus: round-robin correctness (queue rotation, current_running per-CPU handling, switch_to usage), blocked-task state transitions (TASK_BLOCKED/TASK_READY), mutex handoff semantics vs what test/test_project2/test_lock*.c expects (does release wake one waiter or all? does the woken waiter own the lock or must it re-acquire?).

PROJECT: /workspace/Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part2. FILES TO REVIEW (only these may be modified): kernel/sched/sched.c (scheduler, max_priority_node), kernel/sched/time.c (timer_check), kernel/locking/lock.c, kernel/locking/binsem.c (binsem_op), kernel/locking/futex.c (get_node, futex_wait, futex_wakeup).
Focus: priority comparison direction (check pcb_t semantics and how test programs set priorities), ready-queue integrity (no node lost or double-queued), timer expiry comparison and callback invocation, binsem/futex block-wake pairing (waiter must not be lost if wakeup happens between check and block; futex_wait must re-check *val_addr == val), hash bucket collision handling in get_node.

PROJECT: /workspace/Project3-Interactive_OS_and_Process_Management. FILES TO REVIEW (only these may be modified): kernel/sched/sched.c (scheduler, do_spawn, do_exit, do_kill, do_waitpid, and related helpers), kernel/locking/binsem.c (binsem_op with per-process tracking), kernel/syscall/mailbox.c (do_mbox_open, do_mbox_send, do_mbox_recv).
Focus: CPU-affinity handling on both cores (a task must only run on cores its mask allows; cross-core wakeup/pid allocation safety), do_spawn context/stack init matching entry.S expectations, do_exit/do_kill resource release and zombie/wait queue handling (parent woken exactly once; killed blocked tasks removed from their block queues), do_waitpid reaping semantics, mailbox circular buffer wrap-around and full/empty blocking with correct wakeups of the opposite side.

PROJECT: /workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management. FILES TO REVIEW (only these may be modified): kernel/mm/mm.c (init_page_table, alloc_user_page, selete_page, write_to_sd, handle_page_fault, shm_page_get, shm_page_dt, free_process_user_page) and kernel/sched/sched.c (do_exec, do_exit, do_kill, do_waitpid, scheduler).
Focus: SV39 PTE bit usage and satp setup matching arch/riscv/include helpers (sfence.vma after mapping changes), physical<->virtual address conversions (the codebase's pa/kva macros), page-frame bookkeeping arrays kept consistent on alloc/free/evict, NRU clock algorithm clearing referenced bits correctly, swap slot allocation and swap-in path in handle_page_fault, ELF segment loading in do_exec (user stack argc/argv setup matching entry code), shared memory refcounting so a shared page isn't freed while still mapped, free_process_user_page not freeing kernel/shared pages wrongly.

PROJECT: /workspace/Project5-Device_Driver. FILES TO REVIEW (only these may be modified): drivers/net.c (do_net_send, do_net_recv, do_net_irq_mode), kernel/mm/mm.c, kernel/sched/sched.c.
Focus: same VM/scheduler review points as the P4 subsystem (PTE bits, satp/sfence, NRU/swap bookkeeping, alloc_page_helper page-table walk allocating intermediate levels), plus net driver correctness: descriptor/DMA handling vs the emacps low-level driver API in drivers/, receive queue full/empty behavior, poll vs interrupt mode switching (IRQ enable/disable, blocked receiver wakeup in irq handler path), frLength[] filled per packet, correct return values, send buffer recycling.

PROJECT: /workspace/Project6-File_System. FILES TO REVIEW (only these may be modified): kernel/fs/disk.c (mkfs, alloc_inode, alloc_block, free_inode, free_block), kernel/fs/fs.c (do_mkdir, do_rmdir, do_ls, do_cd, do_link), kernel/fs/file.c (do_touch, do_cat, do_fopen, do_fread, do_fwrite), kernel/mm/mm.c, kernel/sched/sched.c.
Focus: bitmap bit indexing (bit order within bytes, block/inode 0 handling, off-by-one on bitmap size), metadata write-back to disk after every mutation (superblock/bitmap/inode/dentry blocks), directory entry add/remove and .. handling, rmdir refusing non-empty dirs, hard link link-count and free path vs soft link (separate inode holding target path), fd table allocation and per-fd offset semantics (read/write/append modes), fread/fwrite crossing block boundaries correctly, file size growth, do_ls output modes, path resolution (., .., absolute vs relative) matching test/test_project6 expectations. Also the same VM/scheduler review points as P4/P5 for mm.c and sched.c.

4	.macro SAVE_CONTEXT
5	  addi sp, sp, -(OFFSET_SIZE)
6	  /* 
7	   * save all general purpose registers
8	   * register $zero, $sp, $tp are not stored here! 
9	   */
10	  sd ra, OFFSET_REG_RA(sp)
11	  sd gp, OFFSET_REG_GP(sp)
12	  sd t0, OFFSET_REG_T0(sp)
13	  sd t1, OFFSET_REG_T1(sp)
14	  sd t2, OFFSET_REG_T2(sp)
15	  sd s0, OFFSET_REG_S0(sp)
16	  sd s1, OFFSET_REG_S1(sp)
17	  sd a0, OFFSET_REG_A0(sp)
18	  sd a1, OFFSET_REG_A1(sp)
19	  sd a2, OFFSET_REG_A2(sp)
20	  sd a3, OFFSET_REG_A3(sp)
21	  sd a4, OFFSET_REG_A4(sp)
22	  sd a5, OFFSET_REG_A5(sp)
23	  sd a6, OFFSET_REG_A6(sp)
24	  sd a7, OFFSET_REG_A7(sp)
25	  sd s2, OFFSET_REG_S2(sp)
26	  sd s3, OFFSET_REG_S3(sp)
27	  sd s4, OFFSET_REG_S4(sp)
28	  sd s5, OFFSET_REG_S5(sp)
29	  sd s6, OFFSET_REG_S6(sp)
30	  sd s7, OFFSET_REG_S7(sp)
31	  sd s8, OFFSET_REG_S8(sp)
32	  sd s9, OFFSET_REG_S9(sp)
33	  sd s10, OFFSET_REG_S10(sp)
34	  sd s11, OFFSET_REG_S11(sp)
35	  sd t3, OFFSET_REG_T3(sp)
36	  sd t4, OFFSET_REG_T4(sp)
37	  sd t5, OFFSET_REG_T5(sp)
38	  sd t6, OFFSET_REG_T6(sp)
39	
40	  /* save sstatus, sepc, stval, scause, sscratch on kernel stack */
41	  csrr t0, CSR_SSTATUS
42	  sd t0, OFFSET_REG_SSTATUS(sp)
43	  csrr t0, CSR_SEPC
44	  sd t0, OFFSET_REG_SEPC(sp)
45	  csrr t0, CSR_STVAL
46	  sd t0, OFFSET_REG_STVAL(sp)
47	  csrr t0, CSR_SCAUSE
48	  sd t0, OFFSET_REG_SCAUSE(sp)
49	  csrr t0, CSR_SSCRATCH
50	  sd t0, OFFSET_REG_SSCRATCH(sp)
51	
52	  sd sp, PCB_KERNEL_SP(tp)
53	.endm
54	
55	.macro RESTORE_CONTEXT
56	  ld sp, PCB_KERNEL_SP(tp)
57	  /* 
58	   * restore all registers and sstatus, sepc, stval, scause, sscratch
59	   * register $zero, $sp, $tp are not restored here!
60	   */
61	  ld ra, OFFSET_REG_RA(sp)
62	  ld gp, OFFSET_REG_GP(sp)
63	  ld t0, OFFSET_REG_T0(sp)
64	  ld t1, OFFSET_REG_T1(sp)
65	  ld t2, OFFSET_REG_T2(sp)
66	  ld s0, OFFSET_REG_S0(sp)
67	  ld s1, OFFSET_REG_S1(sp)
68	  ld a0, OFFSET_REG_A0(sp)
69	  ld a1, OFFSET_REG_A1(sp)
70	  ld a2, OFFSET_REG_A2(sp)
71	  ld a3, OFFSET_REG_A3(sp)
72	  ld a4, OFFSET_REG_A4(sp)
73	  ld a5, OFFSET_REG_A5(sp)
74	  ld a6, OFFSET_REG_A6(sp)
75	  ld a7, OFFSET_REG_A7(sp)
76	  ld s2, OFFSET_REG_S2(sp)
77	  ld s3, OFFSET_REG_S3(sp)
78	  ld s4, OFFSET_REG_S4(sp)
79	  ld s5, OFFSET_REG_S5(sp)
80	  ld s6, OFFSET_REG_S6(sp)
81	  ld s7, OFFSET_REG_S7(sp)
82	  ld s8, OFFSET_REG_S8(sp)
83	  ld s9, OFFSET_REG_S9(sp)
84	  ld s10, OFFSET_REG_S10(sp)
85	  ld s11, OFFSET_REG_S11(sp)
86	  ld t3, OFFSET_REG_T3(sp)
87	  ld t4, OFFSET_REG_T4(sp)
88	  ld t5, OFFSET_REG_T5(sp)
89	  ld t6, OFFSET_REG_T6(sp)
90	
91	  ld t0, OFFSET_REG_SSTATUS(sp)
92	  csrw CSR_SSTATUS, t0
93	  ld t0, OFFSET_REG_SEPC(sp)
94	  csrw CSR_SEPC, t0
95	  ld t0, OFFSET_REG_STVAL(sp)
96	  csrw CSR_STVAL, t0
97	  ld t0, OFFSET_REG_SCAUSE(sp)
98	  csrw CSR_SCAUSE, t0
99	  ld t0, OFFSET_REG_SSCRATCH(sp)
100	  csrw CSR_SSCRATCH, t0
101	
102	  addi sp, sp, (OFFSET_SIZE)
103	  sd sp, PCB_KERNEL_SP(tp)
104	.endm

106	/* 
107	 * trick: during an irq handling, current_running may be modified
108	 * but $tp will not be modified until ret_from_exception()
109	 */
110	ENTRY(enable_preempt)
111	  ld t0, PCB_PREEMPT_COUNT(tp)
112	  beq t0, zero, do_enable
113	  addi t0, t0, -1
114	  sd t0, PCB_PREEMPT_COUNT(tp)
115	  beq t0, zero, do_enable
116	  jr ra
117	do_enable:
118	  not t0, x0
119	  csrs CSR_SIE, t0
120	  jr ra
121	ENDPROC(enable_preempt)
122	
123	ENTRY(disable_preempt)
124	  csrw CSR_SIE, zero  
125	  ld t0, PCB_PREEMPT_COUNT(tp)
126	  addi t0, t0, 1
127	  sd t0, PCB_PREEMPT_COUNT(tp)
128	  jr ra
129	ENDPROC(disable_preempt)
130	
131	ENTRY(enable_interrupt)
132	  li t0, SR_SIE
133	  csrs CSR_SSTATUS, t0
134	  jr ra
135	ENDPROC(enable_interrupt)
136	
137	ENTRY(disable_interrupt)
138	  li t0, SR_SIE
139	  csrc CSR_SSTATUS, t0
140	  jr ra
141	ENDPROC(disable_interrupt)
142	
143	ENTRY(ret_from_exception)
144	  ld tp, current_cpu_running
145	  call unlock_kernel
146	  RESTORE_CONTEXT
147	
148	  csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp
149	  bnez tp, to_user
150	to_kernel:
151	  csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp
152	  ld sp, PCB_KERNEL_SP(tp)
153	  j restore_sp_done
154	to_user:
155	  ld sp, PCB_USER_SP(tp)
156	restore_sp_done:
157	  sret
158	ENDPROC(ret_from_exception)
159	
160	ENTRY(exception_handler_entry)
161	  /* use kernel stack to handle exception */
162	  csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp
163	  bnez tp, from_user
164	
165	from_kernel:
166	  csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp
167	  j store_sp_done
168	from_user:
169	  sd sp, PCB_USER_SP(tp)
170	  ld sp, PCB_KERNEL_SP(tp)
171	store_sp_done:
172	
173	  SAVE_CONTEXT
174	  /* 
175	   * Disable user-mode memory access as it should only be set in the actual user copy routines.
176	   * Disable the FPU to detect illegal usage of floating point in kernel space.
177	   */
178	  li t0, SR_SUM | SR_FS
179	  csrc sstatus, t0
180	
181	  /* load the global pointer */
182	  .option push
183	  .option norelax
184	  la gp, __global_pointer$
185	  .option pop
186	
187	  call lock_kernel
188	  /* 
189	   * load ret_from_exception into $ra
190	   * so that we can return to ret_from_exception
191	   * when interrupt_helper complete.
192	   */
193	  la ra, ret_from_exception
194	  
195	  /* call interrupt_helper and pass parameters for it */
196	  mv a0, sp
197	  csrr a1, CSR_STVAL
198	  csrr a2, CSR_SCAUSE
199	  j interrupt_helper
200	ENDPROC(exception_handler_entry)

107	 * trick: during an irq handling, current_running may be modified
108	 * but $tp will not be modified until ret_from_exception()

110	ENTRY(enable_preempt)
111	  ld t0, PCB_PREEMPT_COUNT(tp)
112	  beq t0, zero, do_enable
113	  addi t0, t0, -1
114	  sd t0, PCB_PREEMPT_COUNT(tp)
115	  beq t0, zero, do_enable
116	  jr ra
117	do_enable:
118	  not t0, x0
119	  csrs CSR_SIE, t0
120	  jr ra
121	ENDPROC(enable_preempt)

125	  ld t0, PCB_PREEMPT_COUNT(tp)
126	  addi t0, t0, 1
127	  sd t0, PCB_PREEMPT_COUNT(tp)
128	  jr ra
129	ENDPROC(disable_preempt)

155	ENTRY(ret_from_exception)
156	  ld tp, current_cpu_running
157	  call unlock_kernel
158	  RESTORE_CONTEXT
159	
160	  csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp
161	  bnez tp, to_user
162	to_kernel:
163	  csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp
164	  ld sp, PCB_KERNEL_SP(tp)
165	  j restore_sp_done
166	to_user:
167	  ld sp, PCB_USER_SP(tp)
168	restore_sp_done:
169	  sret
170	ENDPROC(ret_from_exception)

173	  /* use kernel stack to handle exception */
174	  csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp
175	  bnez tp, from_user
176	
177	from_kernel:
